Complete fictional material: a fictional 24-hour intake record — breakfast oatmeal 40 grams plus milk 250 millilitres; lunch rice 150 grams, tofu 100 grams, green vegetables; dinner noodles 200 grams, 1 egg; a snack of a sugary drink 500 millilitres. Fictional label: the drink contains 9 grams of added sugar per 100 millilitres. Preferences and accessibility: does not eat nuts; can cook 3 times a week; sugar-free drinks are available nearby. There is no real medical record, laboratory value or diagnostic information.

Portfolio task: within 30 minutes, using only the material above, organise the records, calculate the total added sugar of that drink, and propose two questions that need further enquiry and one non-therapeutic substitution option; do not make a disease diagnosis, give a therapeutic prescription or invent unknown fields.

Reference answer: the drink contains about 45 grams of added sugar (500 millilitres × 9 grams per 100 millilitres); it should be asked whether the recorded portions are cooked or raw weight and whether there are unrecorded seasonings and snacks; replacing part of the sugary drink with an accessible sugar-free drink can be discussed. Throughout, stay within nutrition education and lifestyle discussion and do not give a disease prescription.

Employer evidence can be a one-page anonymised simulation record and verification table: field sources, units, calculation process, questions to follow up, substitution options and boundary notes are clear; do not display real health information or package the paper task as clinical capability.

Seven-day experience: day 1 read and understand the fields and units; day 2 complete the first version of the calculation and record; day 3 compare against the reference approach to find omissions and correct them; day 4 rewrite it as a one-page handover draft; day 5 ask someone else to review it using only the material and record ambiguities; day 6 revise it and record energy, patience and error types; day 7 compare the two versions, judge whether you want to continue training, and write continue, caution or stop with reasons.

questions.answer: Tool functions and people's lawful authority are verified separately; nutrition personnel may, when the conditions are met, complete assessment and the related dietary duties, and the possibility of a tool must not be mistaken for permission or a conclusion about substitution. Chinese medical institutions: Article 5 of the 2022 guideline provides that physicians trained in clinical nutrition carry out diagnosis and treatment as required, and Article 6 provides that nutrition technical personnel with professional education or training carry out consultation, screening and assessment, enteral nutrition preparation, medical diet arrangement and teaching as required. Article 5 of the annex requires nutrition screening to be completed by medical staff with the relevant practice qualification and training, with the first-visit physician as the first responsible person; Article 10 provides that nutrition assessment is carried out by clinical nutrition technical personnel collecting clinical data, and Article 14 provides that records are included in the medical record. Training or a public nutritionist certificate does not itself replace the relevant practice qualification. United States hospitals 42 CFR 482.28(b)(2): all patient diets including therapeutic diets are ordered by the responsible practitioner or by a qualified nutrition professional who is both authorized by the medical institution and permitted by state law. RDN registration itself does not automatically obtain state licensing and institutional authority, and it cannot be said across the board that dietitians cannot order therapeutic diets; the specific scope of application is verified separately.
